one_month_reasoning: Inside the window: Q3-26 results ~2026-10-20 (source 35). The headline is already pre-announced (Q3 revenue >20% q/q, raised on 2026-09-21 thanks to the new AI-OEM licence), so the swing factors are Q4 guidance, how much of Q3 royalty is a one-time catch-up vs recurring, backlog/book-to-bill and Gen-2 VPD sampling news. After the Q2 beat the stock fell ~6% (source 10), and it has run ~+37% from ~$223 to $306 in three weeks with insiders filing Form 144 sales on Oct 1-2 (source 11), so I tilt slightly negative (median ~$301) for short-term reversal. Hyperscaler Q3 capex calls (late Oct) are a second event; capex guides have only been raised in 2026 (source 21), mild positive. Spread: ~25% one-month sigma (95% annual vol / 3.5, plus an earnings day), roughly symmetric in log space.

fair_value.method: Blend of NTM P/E (36x Oct-2027 NTM recurring EPS $5.71 = $206), EV/EBITDA (30x NTM EBITDA $364M + $0.5B net cash = $235) and a DCF ($183), weights 0.45/0.35/0.20 = $212, plus ~$1/share of after-tax fixed-licence cash still to be collected = $213. Recurring product+royalty earnings only; one-off settlement and fixed-term licence income excluded from capitalised earnings.

Basis: StockAnalysis forward P/E for all 12 peers on 2026-10-05; forward EV/EBITDA derived consistently as ttm EV/EBITDA / (1 + 3Y EPS CAGR forecast) (BELFB uses revenue CAGR), i.e. approximate NTM. Navitas excluded (unprofitable).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 36x NTM recurring P/E and 30x EV/EBITDA: above the peer medians (27.9x / 22.5x) but inside the ranges and below MPWR (46x / 54x). On the same StockAnalysis basis VICR trades at 56.3x forward P/E, above every peer, and that consensus EPS includes tax benefits and fixed licence income.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Premium: forecast growth is structurally higher (3Y revenue CAGR ~43% vs peer median ~16%; backlog +145% y/y) and ~15% of revenue is high-margin royalty income backed by ITC exclusion orders, while net cash is ~3% of market cap. These should last through the horizon because Fab-1 is sold out into Fab-2 and the second ITC case runs to Sep-2027. Not a full MPWR multiple, because Vicor has heavy customer concentration ('majority of Advanced Products revenue from one or a limited number of customers', 10-K), lost the NVIDIA H100 socket to MPS, faces Infineon-Delta and ADI-Empower VPD entrants, and is capacity-capped until Fab-2. Sell-side outperform calls were not used.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$150 (~30x my 2027 recurring EPS of ~$4.2, under 22x the 2028 estimate) the market would be pricing a lost VPD position or royalty erosion: Gen-2 VPD failing to win production sockets, backlog falling q/q, or an adverse ITC ruling. That would break the growth case rather than reflect ordinary volatility in a 95%-vol stock.

reasoning: Starting facts: Q2-26 revenue $143.4M = product $112.9M + royalty $30.4M, of which $15M came from a fixed $60M two-year licence. Q2 EPS of $1.04 was flattered by a negative tax rate, ~$0.65 normalised. 2025 included a one-off $45M settlement. Mid-September brought a proportional VPD licence with an AI OEM, Q3 guidance raised to >20% q/q, and the stock up ~37% to $305.61. I separated recurring earnings (product plus proportional royalties, ~$90M/yr) from fixed-term or one-off licence cash, which I hold as cash and do not capitalise. The value chain backs demand: MPWR Enterprise Data +164% y/y, Infineon AI power EUR1.5B->2.5B and in allocation, and AI capex base case +50% in 2027. It also shows competition intensifying: MPS took H100, Infineon-Delta co-develop VPD, ADI reportedly bid for Empower. So I model product +37-38% a year capped by Fab-1, giving recurring EPS of $4.17 (2027) and $6.23 (2028) and NTM ~$5.7 at Oct-2027. Against 12 peers (median 27.9x fwd P/E, 22.5x EV/EBITDA) I justify 36x / 30x, inside the ranges, for structurally higher growth and royalty income. Methods give $206 / $235 / $183, so fair value is $213, below the price: the market is capitalising consensus EPS that includes tax benefits and licence catch-ups, plus ITC option value. The distribution is a mixture of bear $140 (25%), base $240 (45%) and bull $430 (30%), lognormal widths 0.30-0.38 consistent with 95% realized vol. Median ~$250, P(>= today) ~36%, with a fat right tail from the Sep-2027 ITC determination and licensing. Research limits: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimates were unavailable (plan or rate limit) and no 2027 VICR consensus EPS was reachable, so 2027-28 figures are my own builds; sec.gov refused scripted access with a generic User-Agent, so filings were read via WebFetch.
